Let \theta=\arcsin\left(\frac{15}{17}\right). The argument \frac{15}{17} is positive, so \theta is an acute angle and can be placed in a right triangle. Call the leg adjacent to \theta x, the leg opposite it y, and the hypotenuse r. Arcsine returns opposite over hypotenuse, so take y=15 and r=17; then x=\sqrt{r^2-y^2}=\sqrt{289-225}=\sqrt{64}=8.

By the right-triangle definitions, \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}, \cos\theta=\frac{x}{r}, \tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}, \csc\theta=\frac{r}{y}, \sec\theta=\frac{r}{x}, and \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}. This expression asks for the cotangent of \theta, so the definition to use is \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}.

With x=8, y=15, and r=17, \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}=\frac{8}{15}.

Therefore \cot\left(\arcsin\left(\frac{15}{17}\right)\right)=\boxed{\frac{8}{15}}.
